---
title: "Ion Solvation"
subtitle: "Stokes–Robinson / Zerres–Prausnitz"
---

## Overview

In concentrated solutions, solvation adjusts the entropy 
of mixing because a non-trivial fraction of solvent molecules 
is removed from the free bulk pool when they form ion 
hydration shells.

## Governing Equations

The excess Gibbs free energy from solvation is:

$$
\frac{\Delta G^{\mathrm{slv}}}{RT}
= n_0 \ln \alpha_0
+ \sum_{i \neq 0} n_i \ln\!\left(\frac{\alpha_i}{\alpha_i^{\infty}}\right)
$$

The average solvation number follows a Langmuir expression:

$$
\bar{h}_i = \frac{N_i k_i x_0^{\mathrm{slv}}}{1 + k_i x_0^{\mathrm{slv}}}
$$
